implementationSummary: Infrastructure/documentation-only implementation of Issue #720: Deploy Celery worker/beat systemd units on VPS. Created two new systemd unit files (juli-celery-worker.service, juli-celery-beat.service) following the existing juli-api.service pattern exactly, updated docs/runbooks/app-review-runbook.md to include new units in install steps and logging section, and updated infra/scripts/env/api.env.example with guidance for enabling Redis/Celery environment variables. Corrected initial spec fidelity violation: removed BindsTo=juli-api.service from both units (handoff required exact pattern match, which uses only After= and Wants=). Units depend on network-online.target and redis-server.service, not on juli-api, maintaining service independence. No changes to application code, deploy scripts, or workflow files.
assumptions: Redis will be provisioned separately on the VPS (package list includes redis-server; unit files assume redis-server.service exists)
DEMO_REFERENCE_SHOP_ID and other environment variables for Celery are already defined or will be set via /etc/juli/api.env
Celery schedule is already defined in backend/src/juli_backend/workers/celery_app.py beat_schedule dict; no custom schedule needed in systemd unit
Operator will manually install units to /etc/systemd/system/ and enable them on VPS (not automated by deploy-release.sh)
risks: BindsTo dependency model: Corrected during review to prevent API restarts from killing in-flight Celery tasks
Redis service name: Assumes 'redis-server.service' exists if redis-server package is installed (standard on Ubuntu); if different service name is used, After= directive needs update
